oauth.notes: GitHub has two types of app: OAuth apps and GitHub Apps. Composio's GitHub auth config uses an OAuth app. This guide is about OAuth apps.

verdict.summary: You fill in a short form. GitHub does not review the app. Later, an organisation owner must approve your app, because new organisations block OAuth apps by default.

whoYouNeed.why: This person registers the app with a personal account.

whoYouNeed.role: An owner or admin of your GitHub organisation (optional)
whoYouNeed.why: You need this person only if the company organisation must own the app.

steps.title: Sign in to GitHub
steps.plain: Sign in to the GitHub account or organisation that will own the app.
steps.whyHuman: You must sign in yourself. After you sign in, an agent can do the next steps.

sources.title: GitHub Docs: Creating an OAuth app

steps.title: Copy the redirect address from Composio
steps.plain: In the Composio dashboard, create a GitHub auth config. Copy the redirect address that it shows. GitHub uses this address to send users back after they click Allow.
steps.technical: Go to Dashboard > Auth Configs > Create Auth Config > GitHub > OAuth2 > Use your own developer credentials. The Composio docs give the address https://backend.composio.dev/api/v3/toolkits/auth/callback. Always use the address that the dashboard shows.

evidence.note: An older Composio guide for Google shows the v1 address (/api/v1/auth-apps/add). Use the address in the dashboard.

steps.title: Register the OAuth app
steps.plain: Fill in the short GitHub form. Give the app name, your website and the redirect address from Composio.
steps.technical: Go to Profile picture > Settings > Developer settings > OAuth apps > New OAuth App. Fill in Application name, Homepage URL and Authorization callback URL. Application description is optional. Keep Enable Device Flow off. You need it only for a command-line sign-in. 'Expire user access tokens' is on by default. For an app that an organisation owns, use https://github.com/organizations/YOUR-ORG/settings/applications/new.

sources.title: GitHub Docs: Creating an OAuth app

link.label: Open GitHub's new OAuth app form

steps.title: Make a client secret and paste it into Composio
steps.plain: On the page of the new app, generate a client secret. Paste the secret and the client ID into the Composio auth config.
steps.whyHuman: The secret is the password for your app. Paste it yourself. Then it does not go into the chat history of an agent.

evidence.note: This is our recommendation. It is not a GitHub rule.

steps.title: Test a connection
steps.plain: Connect a test GitHub account through Composio. Make sure that the approval screen shows the name of your app, not 'Composio'.

nuances.title: All data on the form is public
nuances.detail: GitHub shows the app name, description and home page to users. Do not put internal URLs or private data on the form.
nuances.ifStuck: You can change the app in Developer settings at any time.

sources.title: GitHub Docs: Creating an OAuth app

nuances.title: A user cannot see the repositories of their company
nuances.detail: The organisation of the user has OAuth app restrictions on. New organisations have this setting by default.
nuances.ifStuck: Tell the user to request access from the organisation owner when they connect. Or, the owner can approve the app in the organisation settings.

sources.title: GitHub Docs: OAuth app access restrictions

nuances.title: Limits
nuances.detail: One account or organisation can own a maximum of 100 OAuth apps. Each app can have a maximum of 10 redirect addresses.
nuances.ifStuck: Use one app for each environment. Do not make one app for each customer.

sources.title: GitHub Docs: Creating an OAuth app

config.redirectUriNote: Use the redirect address in your Composio auth config. The Composio docs give https://backend.composio.dev/api/v3/toolkits/auth/callback.

scopes.name: repo
scopes.plain: Read and write all repositories that the user can access, private repositories included.

useCases.label: Read or change code, issues and pull requests
useCases.summary: GitHub does not review the app. Users in an organisation can need approval from the organisation owner.

sources.title: GitHub Docs: Creating an OAuth app

composio.note: Users can connect today through the Composio GitHub app. Use it while you set up your own app. Users see 'Composio' on the approval screen. Other Composio customers share the same rate limits. Polling triggers run a maximum of one time in 15 minutes. Change to your own app when it is ready.

existingApp.summary: Use your existing app. Add the Composio redirect address as one more callback URL. An OAuth app can have a maximum of 10. Paste the client ID and a client secret into Composio. Make a new secret only for Composio. Then you can cancel it and not change your product.

reReviewTriggers.effect: An OAuth app can have a maximum of 10 callback URLs. Remove a callback URL that you do not use, or register a second app.

sources.title: GitHub Docs: Creating an OAuth app

reReviewTriggers.trigger: You want a separate secret for Composio
reReviewTriggers.effect: On the page of the app, you can generate one more client secret. The old secret continues to work until you delete it.

evidence.note: This comes from the GitHub app settings screen. We did not find it on a GitHub docs page.

reReviewTriggers.effect: GitHub does not review the app again. Users give permissions when they connect. They see a new approval screen.

evidence.note: We did not read the GitHub scope docs for this check.

blockers.symptom: Your app sees only the public repositories of an organisation
blockers.cause: New GitHub organisations block OAuth apps by default. Members cannot give your app access to private data until an owner approves the app.
blockers.fix: Tell users about this before they connect. When a user connects, the user requests approval for your app. An organisation owner approves the app in the Third-party access settings of the organisation.

escalate.label: GitHub: how owners approve an OAuth app

sources.title: GitHub: About OAuth app access restrictions
GitHub: Approving OAuth apps for your organization

blockers.cause: The redirect address in the sign-in request is different from the callback URL on your OAuth app.
blockers.fix: Copy the redirect address from your Composio auth config. Paste it exactly into the Authorization callback URL field of the app. Then try again.
